title: Scalping Basics
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/title: What Is Scalping, and Who's It For?
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/0/body: **Scalping** means very short trades, from a few seconds to a few minutes, to catch **small price moves**. A scalper usually works on the **1- to 5-minute** timeframes and takes many trades in a day.
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/1/body: Since each win is small, **one big loss** can wipe out dozens of winning trades. That's why a scalper uses a **tight, non-negotiable stop loss** and never lets a losing trade grow.
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/2/prompt: Which timeframes does a scalper mostly trade on?
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/2/explanati: Scalping chases moves that last minutes, so it works on very low timeframes like the 1- and 5-minute.
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/3/prompt: Here's a scalp setup on the 1-minute chart. How many pips is the take profit from the entry?
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/3/explanati: 1.08560 − 1.08500 = 0.00060, which is 6 pips (1 pip = 0.0001). The stop loss is 4 pips away: a typical scalp setup with a small target and a small risk.
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/4/statement: A scalper usually closes all positions before the trading session ends and holds nothing overnight.
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/4/explanati: A scalper is only in each trade for a few minutes, chasing small moves, so there's no reason to take on overnight risk. Holding overnight is a swing trader's game.
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/5/body: Scalping takes **sharp focus**, **quick decisions** and free time during the market's **most volatile hours**, and it depends on a **low spread** and fast execution from your broker. If you only have time at night, or you get emotional after a loss, slower styles suit you better.
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/5/tip: Try scalping on a demo account first. Its pace is nothing like the other styles.
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/6/prompt: Who is the best fit for scalping?
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/6/options/0: Someone with a few focused hours a day during volatile times
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/6/options/1: An office worker who checks the chart for a few minutes late at night
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/6/options/2: Someone who doubles their size after every loss
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/6/options/3: Someone who likes holding a trade for weeks
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/6/explanati: Scalping means dozens of quick decisions during volatile hours. Limited time, emotional trading after losses, or waiting for weeks-long moves don't fit this style.
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/7/pairs/1/m: Opening and closing the same day
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/8/sentence: On ___ timeframes, a scalper hunts for ___, quick profits.
lessons/scalping-u1-l1/steps/8/explanati: Scalping means catching small moves on the 1- to 5-minute timeframes. Big profits and high timeframes belong to swing trading.
lessons/scalping-u1-l2/steps/0/body: Every trade starts a little in the red: there's the **spread** (the gap between the buy and sell price) and, on some accounts, a **commission**. When your target is only a few pips, that cost eats a **big chunk of your profit**.
lessons/scalping-u1-l2/steps/1/body: The same **1-pip spread** is only **1%** of the target for a swing trader aiming for 100 pips, but **20%** for a scalper aiming for 5. That's why scalpers look for **low-cost accounts** and highly liquid symbols.
lessons/scalping-u1-l2/steps/1/tip: On EUR/USD, 1 pip on 1 lot is about $10, so a $7 commission works out to 0.7 pips.
lessons/scalping-u1-l2/steps/2/prompt: Your scalp target is 8 pips, and spread plus commission come to 2 pips. What percent of the target is the cost?
lessons/scalping-u1-l2/steps/2/explanati: 2 ÷ 8 = 0.25, so a quarter of your target profit goes to costs the moment you enter.
lessons/scalping-u1-l2/steps/3/statement: A 1-pip spread hurts a scalper aiming for 5 pips far more than a swing trader aiming for 100.
lessons/scalping-u1-l2/steps/3/explanati: For the scalper it's 20% of the target, for the swing trader just 1%. The smaller the target, the heavier the cost.
lessons/scalping-u1-l2/steps/4/prompt: You took 20 scalps today, averaging +3 pips gross per trade. If each trade costs 1.5 pips, what's your net profit for the day?
lessons/scalping-u1-l2/steps/4/explanati: Gross: 20 × 3 = 60 pips. Costs: 20 × 1.5 = 30 pips. Net: 60 − 30 = 30 pips. Costs ate half your profit.
lessons/scalping-u1-l2/steps/5/body: Crypto exchanges usually charge a **percentage fee** on volume, like **0.1% per side**. So opening and closing costs about **0.2%** in total. If you're aiming for a 0.3% move, two-thirds of your profit goes to fees.
lessons/scalping-u1-l2/steps/5/tip: During news and thin liquidity, slippage adds to your costs too.
lessons/scalping-u1-l2/steps/6/prompt: The exchange fee is 0.1% per side and your scalp target is a 0.5% move. What percent of your target profit do the round-trip fees eat?
lessons/scalping-u1-l2/steps/6/explanati: The round trip is 0.1 + 0.1 = 0.2%. As a share of the target: 0.2 ÷ 0.5 = 0.4, which is 40%.
lessons/scalping-u1-l2/steps/7/sentence: For a scalper, a low ___ is vital, because each trade only aims for a few ___.
lessons/scalping-u1-l2/steps/7/explanati: When your target is only a few pips, every tenth of a pip of spread eats a big percentage of your profit.
lessons/scalping-u1-l2/steps/8/pairs/0/m: The gap between buy and sell price
lessons/scalping-u1-l2/steps/8/pairs/2/m: An order filled at a worse price
lessons/scalping-u1-l2/steps/8/pairs/3/m: The exchange fee on a market order
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/0/body: A scalper needs two things: **high liquidity** (low spread and fast execution) and **enough volatility** (price actually moving). In forex, these two usually come together in the **London session** and the **London–New York overlap**.
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/0/tip: These hours are approximate and shift a little when daylight saving time starts and ends.
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/1/prompt: The first candles are from the end of the Asian session and the rest from the London open. Which part is better for scalping?
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/1/options/0: Second part: more movement and volume
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/1/explanati: When London opened, volume multiplied and candles got longer, so there's both liquidity and movement. In the quiet part, candles barely move more than the cost of a trade.
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/2/body: For a few minutes **before and after major news** (like NFP and CPI), the spread widens and slippage is high. Around **rollover** (about 17:00 New York time), spreads usually widen too. And **quiet** hours don't move enough to cover your costs.
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/3/statement: Right at the moment major news is released, the spread usually shrinks, making it the best time to scalp.
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/3/explanati: During news, liquidity providers step back: the spread widens and price jumps. Many scalpers don't trade for a few minutes before and after a release.
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/4/prompt: For scalping EUR/USD, which time window is usually best?
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/4/explanati: During the overlap, two big financial centers are active at once, so liquidity is high and the spread is low. Midnight is quiet, and the news minute and rollover bring wide spreads.
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/5/statement: Even though crypto trades 24/7, liquidity is usually lower on weekends than on weekdays.
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/5/explanati: The market never closes, but volume usually picks up with European and US active hours and drops on weekends. For a scalper, that means wider spreads and more slippage.
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/6/prompt: Put the routine for a scalping session in order.
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/6/items/1: Mark the key levels on your chart
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/6/items/2: Trade once the volatile hours begin
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/6/items/3: Pause a few minutes before major news
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/6/items/4: End the session when volatility fades
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/6/explanati: First you find out what news is due today, then you prep your chart map, trade only during volatile hours, step aside around news, and stop once the market goes quiet.
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/7/prompt: It's 13:25 London time, and US CPI comes out in 5 minutes. You've also spotted a scalp setup on the 1-minute. What do you do?
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/7/options/0: Wait until the news is out and the spread is back to normal
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/7/options/1: Go in with bigger size since volatility is coming
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/7/options/2: Enter without a stop loss so a spike doesn't close me out
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/7/options/3: Enter and don't look at the chart until after the news
lessons/scalping-u1-l3/steps/7/explanati: US CPI usually comes out at 8:30 New York time (about 13:30 in London). A setup taken 5 minutes before the news is really a bet on the news, not a scalp.
